label: copy-phase input m (fed-back m at recall_idx >= 3)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is m (97% of activation mass on in_tok == m; zero activation in original/delimiter phases, so an m in the original sequence never triggers it). Gated by position: m echoed at recall_idx 0-1 never fires and at recall_idx 2 rarely does; strong at recall_idx >= 3, i.e. when the m came from original position >= 3. Top activations (~0.9-1.0 of max) are m inputs late in the copy of long sequences; m echoed at original position 2 gives weaker activations (~0.3-0.6). Remaining ~29k active steps not on m are tiny (mostly <0.1 of max, 4% of mass), scattered over arbitrary copy-phase tokens, often right after an m. Does not depend on the output token or on the first token.

issues: Core claims hold on test. The original predicate gives P 0.931, R 0.648, F1 0.764, mass recall 0.957. The feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases (0 active steps in the profile). in_tok==m holds 0.970 of the activation mass. An m at recall_idx 2 gives P 0.14 and mass 0.012, and recall_idx 0-1 never fires.

There is one small systematic false-positive pocket the explanation does not mention: m at recall_idx==3 in long sequences. On test, precision is 1.0 for L=4, 1.0 for L=5, 0.92 for L=6, 0.63 for L=7, 0.45 for L=8 and 0.56 for L=9. This is about 2.4k of the 4k false positives. Excluding (recall_idx==3)&(L>=7) raises precision to 0.996, but F1 drops slightly to 0.743, so the original predicate is still the better trade-off.
The firing threshold tracks recall_idx, not closeness to the end. For m inputs, recall_idx>=4 gives precision 1.0. Within recall_idx>=3, to_go only reflects L.

The explanation says leftover activations land 'often right after an m'. That is overstated: only about 5.5% of active steps are non-m inputs with prev_tok==m (P 0.06). Most of the residual, 21.7% of active steps, comes in sequences where no m has been seen at all. The residual is scattered low-magnitude noise spread over all tokens (bottom activation quartile coverage is only 0.087), consistent with the 4% mass.

The explanation says an m copied from an earlier position gives a weaker activation (it was not scored). This is not supported. Repeated m (in_count>1) has precision 0.92 and a mass-to-step ratio of about 1.5, the same as single-occurrence m (about 1.47). There is no clear weakening.
